    "Leave-one-observation-out"-like predictions by zeroing each positive case in a brms model

    predict_as_zero_loo.Rd

    This function performs the follow: for every row in the model data where `interaction_col == 1`, the value of that row is temporarily set to 0, and the model is re-updated. It then computes the predictor (on the specified `scale`) for the modified observation. This can be used to quantify how individual positive observations contribute to the fitted model.

    predict_as_zero_loo(
  model,
  interaction_col = "interaction",
  cores = 2,
  iter = 1000,
  warmup = 500,
  chains = 1,
  recompile = FALSE,
  scale = "linear"
)

    Arguments

    model

    A `brmsfit` object containing an attached data list (i.e., `model$data` must exist).

    interaction_col

    A single character string giving the name of the binary column to perturb when generating 1-to-0 predictions. Defaults to 'interaction'.

    cores

    Integer. Number of parallel workers to use. Defaults to 2.

    iter

    Integer. Total number of sampling iterations for each refitted model. Defaults to 1000.

    warmup

    Integer. Number of warmup iterations for each refitted model. Defaults to 500.

    chains

    Integer. Number of chains to run for each refitted model. Defaults to 1.

    recompile

    Logical. Passed to `brms::update()` to control whether the underlying Stan model is recompiled on each iteration.

    scale

    A single character string passed to `brms::fitted()`, indicating the scale of the response variable. Defaults to 'linear'.

    Value

    A data frame with one row per positive observation. Columns: * `row_no`: the index of the row modified, * `pred`: the predicted estimate for the modified row.

    Details

    Computation is parallelised across the number of workers specified by `cores`.

    This approach is similar in spirit to leave-one-out cross-validation, except that the row is not removed; instead, its value in `interaction_col` is set to 0 and the model is refit to estimate the corresponding counterfactual prediction.

    Examples

    if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
results <- predict_as_zero_loo(
  model = my_brms_model,
  interaction_col = "interaction",
  cores = 4
)
} # }
